//: Firebase Hosting config for the outlet PWA. Note apps/api/firebase.json is a
SEPARATE, unrelated file that configures only the local Auth emulator — this
one is the deploy config and is used from the repo root.
The /api/** rewrite is load-bearing, not a convenience. packages/api-client
hardcodes a relative API_BASE ('/api/v1') so a Firebase bearer token can
never be sent cross-origin. That only holds if the API answers on the SAME
origin as the app, which this rewrite is what accomplishes: the browser sees
one origin, Hosting forwards /api/** to Cloud Run server-side. Point the app
at an absolute API URL instead and you reintroduce exactly the cross-origin
token exposure the relative base exists to prevent.
Rewrite ORDER matters: the SPA catch-all below would swallow /api/** if it
came first, and the failure mode is index.html returned with a 200 where
JSON was expected.
Vite emits content-hashed filenames for everything under /assets, so a
given URL's bytes never change — immutable is safe and means repeat
visits on a patchy mobile connection re-fetch nothing.
The service worker and its registration shim must NOT be cached. These
filenames are stable across builds, so a cached copy pins a device to
an old precache manifest — the update prompt (src/pwa/UpdatePrompt.jsx)
would then never fire, and a cashier stays on a stale build
indefinitely. This is the one file where a cache hit is a bug.
index.html is the entry point that references the hashed assets; caching
it would serve old asset URLs after a deploy.

headers.//: Baseline hardening. The API sets its own headers on /api/** responses.
